prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: finished watercolor concept art for a continuous side-scrolling 2D puzzle-platformer level, Level 04 "Shallow Reservoir — Leave the Weight, Carry the Light".
Create ONE wide landscape illustration, about 2.2:1 aspect ratio, high detail, full-bleed scene. No labels, no text, no UI, no arrows, no storyboard panels.

REFERENCE ROLES:
Image 1 is ONLY the spatial and mechanism layout reference. Translate the central map into believable garden architecture; do not render any of its diagram typography, lines, numbered circles, borders, ghost states or bottom cards.
Image 2 is the approved ART STYLE: richly illustrated watercolor on textured paper, soft pigment blooms, delicate dark hand-drawn outlines, mossy ochre masonry, blue-green ivy, gentle golden sunlight, quiet storybook atmosphere. Keep this painterly 2D illustration style, NOT photoreal/PBR and NOT a vector diagram.
Image 3 is ONLY the design of the little wick spirit. Show it very small within the level, only one character.

CAMERA AND SCALE:
Straight-on orthographic side elevation, camera perpendicular to the garden retaining wall. A single horizontal gameplay plane. No isometric view, no top-down courtyard. Walkable top edges read as clean lateral platforms with visible vertical masonry faces. Background foliage/wall is softer and slightly recedes; only a shallow hint of top surface on stonework. A miniature world at the foot of an abandoned garden wall: moss stems, leaf veins, old terracotta shards and roots feel large relative to a tiny luminous spirit. Character total height about 4 percent of image height, with an oversized ivory flame-shaped head and tiny body.

CONTINUOUS SPATIAL COMPOSITION:
Left shore occupies approximately x0–23%; dry middle island x40–59%; right shore x79–100%. Ground tops align around 68% of image height. Between them are TWO distinct broad water gaps, both far beyond the tiny character's normal jump range. Blue-green still shallow pool, subtle ripples and warm beam reflections, visible submerged roots. No stepping stones or floating-leaf bridge bridging either water gap.
Left edge: a mossy old drain arch opening from level03, sitting on the left bank. In the upper-left old plaster-and-brick wall is a narrow break admitting a clear slanted shaft of sunlight.
Middle: rooted, moss-clad masonry island, clean walkable top. Three small fixed root-and-pottery ledges climb diagonally up-right behind the left half of this island to a high botanical storage trough at about x54%, y35%. These are believable short-jump supports, not a continuous staircase spanning the water. Empty upper trough has a lip on both ends and a single bottom outlet.
At x64%, beyond the island, a dense narrow VERTICAL ROOT SCREEN descends from the overhead root arbor all the way into the water. It is a continuous opaque obstacle, no walkable top, no way for a full-sized spirit to pass. Its one tiny horizontal aperture aligns exactly with the main light beam. A separate leaf shutter can cover that aperture; show it LIFTED above the aperture in this scene.
Right: mossy shore with an old pump-house wall and pipe-mouth exit at the far right. Behind its walkable bank, show only a cropped patch of the enormous immobile creature's lower belly emerging from earth and masonry, continuing out of the right frame. Soft ivory-white overlapping organic scales. NO creature face, whole animal, egg, detached tail or freestanding rock. One distinct charcoal-gray feeding scale sits within the pale belly patch, visible above the bank; its center receives the first touch of gold light while its darker outline remains evident.

DRAW THE FINAL CONNECTED PUZZLE STATE, WITH PLAUSIBLE PHYSICAL CONNECTIONS:
1. A small FIXED tilted reflective shard, held in a natural stone/root bracket on the left bank, receives sunlight from the upper-left crack. It reflects ONE golden beam perfectly horizontally to the right, at approximately y62%, a little above the walkable surface.
2. On the middle island, a broad low hinged wooden/leaf pressure treadle. Its LEFT SIDE is a shallow independent cup containing exactly ONE brown heavy seedpod. The seedpod presses the plate and is entirely below the beam. The RIGHT SIDE leaves a clear empty standing/charging place for the little spirit. Show the ONE tiny spirit beside the terminal mirror on the RIGHT BANK, having completed the crossing. Do not duplicate the seedpod in the upper trough.
3. A fixed concave root chute descends from the high empty seed trough to a pivoting green guide-leaf ramp. Show this guide leaf FOLDED UP, entirely above the main beam, with a clearly visible hinge and small reachable control handle at island ground level. The ramp is a broad veined leaf with raised curled edges, distinct from the distant shutter. Its lowered position would have connected to the seed cup and blocked the beam, but DO NOT draw a transparent ghost of this position.
4. A visible thin brown fibrous rope from the treadle routes up the rear side of the middle island over TWO small natural wooden pulley wheels near the overhead arbor, then down to the lifted leaf shutter on the root screen. Plausible weight linkage, neat continuous rope, no giant industrial machine. Ropes are matte brown, do not glow, and remain visually separate from the golden beam.
5. The uninterrupted horizontal beam crosses the first water gap, the island charging place, the tiny OPEN aperture in the root screen, and the second water gap to a small adjustable reflective shard mounted on a root pivot on the right bank. Only at this terminal mirror does the beam turn diagonally UP-RIGHT to the dark feeding scale in the pale beast belly.

VISUAL HIERARCHY:
Quiet warm watercolor garden, serene and poetic, soft pale sunlight above, cooler translucent water below. Plenty of airy readable space around the beam and mechanisms, avoid clutter at the play surface. Interactive props and playable ledge edges have slightly stronger fine ink contours and a restrained pale rim highlight. Light is a thick enough warm golden shaft with soft halo; ropes are clearly narrower rough brown fibers. Background has no competing bright ray. A few foreground roots at bottom corners only, never covering the walking path, water gaps or mechanisms. Upper canopy roots and ivy belong to the garden wall, with gentle atmosphere and paper grain. No modern lamps, spotlights, floating mechanical controls, instructional text, duplicate character, or extra optical branches. This must look like an evocative finished game scene, while faithfully preserving the three-bank level topology.
